entityName: Sieć Badawcza ŁUKASIEWICZ - Instytut Spawalnictwa; ŁUKASIEWICZ Research Network - Institute of Welding
entityDescription:
Established in 1945, Instytut Spawalnictwa (since 1st April 2019 Sieć Badawcza Łukasiewicz - Instytut Spawalnictwa) is a leading and key welding research and development organisation in Poland. In its long-standing activity Instytut Spawalnictwa has been solving problems in welding technology, coordinated numerous R&D projects and strengthened close links with the Polish industry and foreign centres. It's scope of activities covers issues concerning processes of joining structural materials with the use of advanced technologies of welding, brazing, thermal cutting and allied technologies. Instytut Spawalnictwa is the only organisation of its type in Poland and functions as:

- ANB - Authorised National Body - in European Federation for Welding, Joining and Cutting (EWF) and International Institute of Welding - authorised for qualification of welding personnel,
- ANBCC - Authorised National Body for Company Certification in EWF and IIW - authorised for certification of enterprises according to the PN-EN ISO 3834 standard,
- Accredited in Polish Centre for Accreditation (PCA) organisation for certification of welding processes, Factory Production Control, welding and NDT personnel and quality management systems,
- Notified Body in the European Union in the scope of 2014/68/EU Directive and Regulation (EU) no. 305/2011 of the European Parliament and of the council 

Mission - development and transfer of knowledge in the field of joining advanced structural materials in order to ensure innovation and competitiveness of producers of welded structures

entityDescription:
Open Climate Fix is a new non-profit research and development lab, totally focused on reducing greenhouse gas emissions as rapidly as possible. Every part of the organisation is designed to maximise climate impact, such as our open and collaborative approach, our rapid prototyping, and our attention on finding scalable & practical solutions.

By using an open-source approach, we can draw upon a much larger pool of knowledge and skills than any individual company, so combining existing islands of knowledge and accelerating progress. Our approach will be to search for ML (Machine Learning) problems where, if we solve a well-defined ML task, then there's likely to be a large climate impact.
Then, for each of these challenges, we'll:

1. Collate & release data, and write software tools to make it super-easy for people to consume this data.
2. Run a collaborative 'global research project' where everyone from 16-year-olds to PhD students to corporate research labs can help solve the ML tasks.
3. Help to put good solutions into production, once the community has developed them, so we can be reducing emissions ASAP.

entityDescription:
CAMEA, spol. s r. o., (CAMEA) is engaged in the development and production of modern image and signal processing systems for industrial use, road monitoring and other applications.
CAMEA is active in the following areas:
• research into methods and algorithms of image processing and computer vision,
• research in the field of computer graphics and human-computer interaction,
• research of image sensors and signal processing with acceleration by technical means,
• design of tools and subsystems for image processing and signal processing,
• design of turnkey systems and solutions using research results,
• manufacture and sale of image sensors and image processing equipment.

CAMEA was founded in 1995 by a group of professionals working in the field of image processing, computer graphics and signal processing at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Brno University of Technology (Czech Republic). It has undergone major developments since 1995 and is currently focusing on two basic areas:
• industrial camera systems;
• intelligent transport systems.

In addition to systems and custom solutions, CAMEA's activities include research and development, production and sale of video and signal processing components such as camcorders, digitizing boards for PCs, stand-alone microprocessor boards for control and stand-alone boards with signal processors for control purposes and image and signal processing. The company is also engaged in creating programming tools and subsystems for working with images and signal processing in real time.
Following state-of-art trends and in-house research and development, it is today a leading manufacturer of highly innovative solutions for these two areas.

CAMEA products are at the top of image processing technology in the Czech Republic. It has pioneered the measurement of segment speed and high-speed vehicle weighing. Exports abroad have also increased significantly in the last approximately 7 years. In foreign markets, we are talking about acting on B2B markets. CAMEA intends to build a global network of business partners representing its technology solutions in the regions. This format has already proven itself in the Russian Federation and the East African region.

entityDescription:
Holistic Innovation, S.L.U. (HI2), is a Spanish SME, specialized on services associated to the innovation management for the research and technology development with specific focus on spectrum management affairs, while bearing a holistic and strategic vision for the businesses associated to the research, technology development and innovation in the fields of audiovisual, networked media, future internet, satellite communications, earth observation, mobile communications, eHealth and maritime communications. HI´s staff, headed by Dr. Julián Seseña:
•	Has a particular experience in the field of spectrum management, standardization and policy development.
•	Provides services and associated commitment to reach objectives and flexibility to adapt to the evolving business and technology world, through setting close team with our customers.
•	Counts with spectrum mnagement professionals and researchers who offer many years’ experience on research in the fields of networked media, satellite communications, specific challenges associated to SMEs and eHealth, as well as strategic, regulatory and policy initiatives.
The well experienced staff of the company has participated in many European, National and International Cooperation Projects, as well as on activities of DVB, ETSI, ITU, Networld2020, NEM, ISI, GVF, CENELEC, ECC and is fully aware on the current trends on standardization, regulation, policy and ICT network infrastructure. 
 
HI´s staff is involved usually at the CETP meetings and is deeply aware of the activities of the ECC, CEPT WG FM, PT FM 44, PT FM50, PT FM45, WG SE, PT SE19, PT SE40, etc., monitoring also the international trends in Spectrum management, including activities of the European Radio Spectrum Committee, European Radio Spectrum Policy Group and the preparatory activities towards World Radiocommunications Conferences at European and ITU levels.

entityName: STICHTING NEDERLANDSE WETENSCHAPPELIJK ONDERZOEK INSTITUTEN / CWI. CENTRUM WISKUNDE & INFORMATICA
entityDescription:
Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI) is the national research institute for mathematics and computer science in the Netherlands. Founded in 1946, CWI is part of the Institutes Organisation of NWO, NWO-I since January 1st, 2018. 
While located at Amsterdam Science Park, our institute has strong international links, and we enjoy a global reputation for our innovative research.
At CWI, our strength is discovering and developing new ideas that benefit society and the economy, as well as other scientific areas. Our research is rooted in practical, real-life questions and explores essential aspects of modern life, including transport and communication networks, internet security, medical imaging and smart energy systems. 
Our innovations form an integral part of numerous software products, programming languages and international standards. CWI is at the heart of European research in mathematics and computer science. We take part in many international programmes, including EU Horizon2020 and EIT Digital. 
With close ties to industry and the wider academic world, both at home and abroad, we maintain a sharp focus on the bigger picture and real-world issues. The institute was the birthplace of the European internet in 1988. We registered one of the first country domains in the world, .nl, in 1986. We built the first Dutch computer in 1952 and kick-started the development of the popular programming language Python in the 1990s. So far, CWI has founded 26 spin-off companies.

We built the first Dutch computer in 1952 and kick-started the development of the popular programming language Python in the 1990s. So far, CWI has founded 26 spin-off companies.

entityDescription:
GL BIOCONTROL specializes in environmental risk management and has an expertise in sanitary engineering along with biological monitoring of water and surfaces.
Our clients are environment professionals: industrialists, industry operators, water treatment companies, laboratories, study design engineer and public authorities.
We have several skills including: studies, research and development, analysis, product development and professional training. Through these areas of expertise, 
GL BIOCONTROL:
•	Develops risk management tools (ATP-metry kits for total flora quantification, DNA extraction purification kits, real time PCR amplification kits…).
•	Uses methodologies and innovative tools to study the microbial world (qPCR, NGS, ATP-metry…).
•	Studies ecosystems to anticipate and prevent public health risks, in particular linked to Legionella and Pseudomonas genus (risk assessment, microbiology diagnostics, ATP cartography…).
•	Advises water sector professionals on how to manage their facilities in order to reduce public health risks as well as improve the environmental footprint (water, treatment products and energy conservation).
•	Trains environmental professionals on microbiological risk management and laboratory techniques.
